definition.proposition: On the all-parts backbone A3mx at 200M tokens of code-py-v2, replacing the 8k-way BPE output head with a tokens-as-patches byte decoder (d_local 128, shared refinement r_b = 2, A4a) costs about 14% in val nats per target token, so the full stack is not viable by A4's registered rule (within 3% of A3mx).

scope.dataset: code-py-v2 val split (in-training eval, nats per target token incl. EOT; not clean80)
scope.architecture: A3mx trunk + gogeta/c2f.py byte decoder (A4a) vs A3mx BPE head
scope.model_size: d=384 trunk, d_local 128 decoder, 25.7M total params

definition.refutation_criteria: REFUTED if clean80 bits per char (SQ387) puts A4a within 3% of A3mx, or a tuned-LR replication's paired 95% CI upper bound is <= +3%

qual: 3 seeds, registered; metric not clean80 (SQ387); LR not bracketed
reason: R1: A4a - A3mx = +14.39%, paired 95% CI [+13.39, +15.39], df 2, dz +38.1, seeds 5-7; prediction +2% (-2% to +6%): OUT of range. Viability rule (CI upper <= +3%) fails. Not VERIFIED because the registered metric is the in-training v2 val (not clean80, policy 2.2) and the decoder arms ran at an unbracketed 6e-3. EOT costs 0.072 nats per token of the gap; without it A4a is still about +7%.
